candidate.title: NOMe-Seq
candidate.scope: The central NOMe-Seq row of the supplied Illumina poster: accessibility-dependent GpC methylation of chromatin followed by a bisulfite DNA sequencing readout, including its Control comparator. The left overview cartoon is descriptive, not an additional transformation. Adjacent partial MINCE-seq, FAIRE-seq/Sono-Seq and histone methylation rows belong to other poster entries. The matching collection page confirms NOMe-Seq scope. The extraction describes the schematic core, not every implementation of NOMe-seq; library construction remains broad and the comparator preparation is unspecified.

evidence.quote: To generate integrated DNA methylation and nucleosome occupancy information, nuclei are treated with M.CviPI, which methylates GpC dinucleotides not protected by nucleosomes or tight binding proteins.

Following bisulfite conversion to differentiate between methylated and unmethylated cytosine residues, cytosines contained within a CpG dinucleotide context provide endogenous methylation information, while nucleosome positioning is derived from cytosines within GpC dinucleotides.
Importantly, both pieces of epigenetic information are obtained from the same individual DNA molecule, revealing the relationship between these two chromatin features on a single chromosome.

states.label: M.CviPI-treated bisulfite sequence readout
features: Additional red sites occur in exposed intervals; gray Protected intervals retain unmarked sites and can also contain endogenous methylated sites.
GpC accessibility and CpG endogenous methylation are distinguished by sequence context on the same DNA-derived read.
Protected/unprotected and methylated/unmethylated describe independent axes, yielding four chromatin signatures.
GpC availability limits footprint sampling; protection is not uniquely diagnostic of a nucleosome because tight binding proteins can also block M.CviPI.
GCG sites confound the two methylation sources; the primary paper separates interpretable sequence contexts.

Source endpoint labels are Protected methylated, Unprotected methylated, Protected unmethylated, and Unprotected unmethylated. Their interpretation requires distinguishing endogenous CpG status from GpC methylation added by the enzyme; a red treated marker is not by itself a CpG-specific signal.
Co-occurrence of accessibility and endogenous methylation is supported within the sequenced DNA span; the schematic does not identify the cell of origin of each read.
Ordinary BS-Seq does not distinguish endogenous 5mC from 5hmC.
The terminal blue tracks have black or red arrowheads but no chemical DNA end-group, adapter or strand-polarity labels.

operations.label: GpC methyltransferase (M.CviPI) and S-Adenosyl methionine (SAM)
operations.description: Act on nucleosome-containing chromatin to add GpC methylation at enzyme-accessible DNA while protected sites remain comparatively unmodified.
operations.mechanism: M.CviPI is the catalytic reagent and SAM is supplied for methylation. Accessibility-dependent methylation changes DNA rather than isolating or sequencing nucleosomes.
operations.information_effect: Covalent methylation writes a chromatin accessibility footprint onto genomic DNA alongside the pre-existing CpG methylation information.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion BS-Seq
operations.description: Treated branch: convert the methylation-marked genomic DNA into bisulfite DNA that distinguishes methylated from unmethylated cytosines. The paper clarifies that DNA is extracted after footprinting; extraction is not a separate depicted block.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite conversion distinguishes cytosine methylation states; the bound proteins are not the sequenced analyte.
operations.information_effect: The added GpC footprint and endogenous CpG information remain associated through their shared DNA sequence. The source reports conversion-dependent C/T sequence calls; it does not use a nucleosome fragment-enrichment read count as the direct carrier of this footprint.

corrections.diagram_observation: Both chromatin cartoons have CpG dinucleotides / Methylated CpG legends. The enzyme caption instead specifies GpC methyltransferase. The M.CviPI endpoint adds red sites in exposed intervals, including a red site addressed by Unprotected unmethylated. No separate marker style is supplied for introduced GpC methylation versus endogenous CpG methylation.
corrections.primary_statement: The primary paper assigns endogenous methylation to CpG context and the enzymatically introduced accessibility footprint to GpC context; protected GpCs resist the enzyme. Figure 1A describes four combinations of endogenous methylation and nucleosome protection. The treated-readout state is authored using this distinction: an exposed region with unmethylated endogenous CpGs may nevertheless carry methylated GpCs after treatment. The diagram wording and symbol pattern are retained, without interpreting every red site as endogenous CpG or interpreting the lower red site as chemically unmethylated after labeling.
